verdict.rationale: Windmill documents a low-code flow builder for assembling multi-step flows, with branching and per-step retries. However, the flow steps are functions written in code (TypeScript, Python, etc.), so the builder is low-code rather than no-code, and an ops user would likely still need to write or reuse scripts. Missing for 10: evidence of a fully no-code step library or pre-built integrations, a detailed description of the visual flow editor, and hands-on corroboration from non-developer users.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can build multi-step workflows in a visual editor without writing code

citations.quote: An orchestrator for assembling these functions into efficient, low-latency flows, using either a low-code builder or YAML
Windmill supports both UI-based operations via its webIDE and low-code builders
Scripts are turned into sharable UIs automatically, and can be composed together into flows
Branches allow to split the execution of the flow based on a condition.
